notes: These records name Li Cunxu, Zhuangzong, Tang Zhuangzong, or Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang and consistently describe the Prince of Jin who founded Later Tang and reigned from AD 923 to 926.

Liao Shi 1 abbreviates the name as Li Cun in the AD 917 entry. Liao Shi 2 identifies that same Li Cun as the Prince of Jin who proclaimed Tang in AD 923 and as the ruler killed by Guo Cunqian before Li Siyuan's accession in AD 926; those events uniquely identify Li Cunxu.

The shared form xiao'er (the boy or young son) is contextual rather than a personal name. Xin Wudai Shi 38 refers to Li Cunxu, Jiu Wudai Shi 62 to a young son of Dong Zhang, and Nan Qi Shu 55 to an unrelated boy of Shan County.
